reports.summary:
• Verdict: the internet was reliable in October. The watchdog ran 5038 checks and showed 99.9% WAN uptime, with no measured outages, no downtime and no automatic restarts. Nothing worrying stood out.
• The router logged 1 WAN disconnect with 2 reconnect cycles (init, connecting, connected), but the LAN-side watchdog measured no outage, so any interruption was too brief to register. There were no router reboots, and peak router memory use was 66.5%.
• The line performed consistently across 18 speedtests: download averaged 933.5 Mbps (minimum 929.5) and upload averaged 302.8 Mbps. Ping averaged 7.08 ms (maximum 31.14 ms), jitter averaged 0.27 ms, and line quality never dropped below 96.7%.
• There is no comparison with September. The watchdog recorded no checks then, and speedtests, traffic and DNS data were not collected for that month. DNS filtering stats were also not collected for October.
• Traffic data covers only 1 of 31 days (Oct 31), so October totals and rankings aren't meaningful yet. The top-listed devices on that day were plex.local, an unnamed Proxmox Server Solutions device, Smart display, TV 3 and Speaker 1. On average 31.8 clients were connected, with a peak of 38.
• 8 new devices appeared:
• Laptop 3 (Oct 14)
• an unnamed Amazon device and a Garmin "WILC" device (Oct 15)
• three WiZ bulbs (Oct 16)
• Air purifier, a Xiaomi device (Oct 25)
• Smart plug, an Espressif device (Oct 26)

  This looks like normal smart-home growth, and no security-relevant events were flagged.
• Recommendation: confirm that the unnamed Amazon device and the Garmin "WILC" device are yours, then give them clear names. Consider doing the same for the unnamed Proxmox device that appears under the "Other" network.
